Wizard Arena

Restore the balance · drug interactions

Longest runs

The ten longest survival runs players chose to post, from every device — ranked by medications balanced, then by points.

How it works. Each medication shows up with its level out of the therapeutic window. You see the drug’s name, never its pathway, and your four throws show only their names.
  • Too weak? Throw something that inhibits the enzyme clearing it. Too strong? Throw an inducer.
  • A strong perpetrator moves the meter two notches, a moderate one moves it one, and a weak one barely flickers — so a strong throw can overshoot.
  • Wrong enzyme: no effect. Wrong direction: it gets worse. Every turn it ends out of the window, it hits you.
  • Lithium, valproate and lamotrigine don’t play by CYP rules at all.
Throwing a drug to fix a level is the game’s conceit — in practice nobody adds a medication to correct another’s level. Each result card explains why the interaction matters when the two end up prescribed together, and how the label adjusts the dose.
Keys: 1–4 to throw, Space to skip text.
Strengths follow the FDA’s table of drugs that interact with CYP enzymes (May 2026); dose advice follows each drug’s label  •  a game, not a prescribing guide — educational use only
Too weakWindowToo strong
▼
How to play
  • The meter shows the medication’s level. Get the marker into the green window.
  • Too weak? Throw something that inhibits the enzyme that clears it. Too strong? Throw an inducer.
  • Strong perpetrators move the meter two notches, moderate ones one, and weak ones only flicker — so a strong throw can overshoot.
  • Wrong enzyme: no effect. Wrong direction: it gets worse. Each turn that ends outside the window, the medication hits you (2 HP when it’s far out).
  • Lithium, valproate and lamotrigine aren’t cleared by CYP enzymes — think kidney and glucuronidation instead.
  • After each battle the card shows every throw’s real pathway and strength, and why the interaction matters clinically.
  • Keys: 1–4 to throw, Space or a tap on the text box to skip ahead.
Educational use only. Medications should generally not be used to change the concentration of other medications, except in rare situations. This game is meant for board review, not as clinical guidance.

Wizard's Escape

Cast fast · Cast true · Get out

The situation

You are locked in a haunted castle. Every room's exit is blocked by three identical hiding places — you cannot tell them apart by looking, only by the answer written on each. Shatter the right one and the way opens. Miss and the spell fizzles: no points lost, but the clock keeps running, and a slow spell is a weak spell.

Wizards

Optional. Opens a room so players tap 1, 2 or 3 on their own phone instead of sharing a keyboard. In survival, everyone who joins runs together.
